Transformer Parameters

Transformer & PQ Formulas:
• Turns Ratio:
a = Vp / Vs

• Reflected Resistance:
Rp = Rs × a²

• Primary Power Calculation:
MW = (Secondary W × PT × CT) / 1,000,000

Plant Capacity / MD to Secondary Current

3-Phase Current Calculation Formulas:
• From MW:
I_primary = (MW × 10⁶) / (√3 × V_kV × 1000 × PF)

• From MD (MVA):
I_primary = (MVA × 10⁶) / (√3 × V_kV × 1000)

• Secondary CT Current:
I_sec = I_primary / CT_ratio

Power Calculator

AC Single Phase Power Formula:
• Apparent Power (S):
kVA = (V × I) / 1000

• Real Power (P):
kW = kVA × cos θ

• Reactive Power (Q):
kVAR = √(S² - P²)

Transformer Power — Formulas & Calculator

Enter values in the formula box you need, then tap Calculate. Use line voltage and line current for the balanced three-phase formulas below.

1. Single-Phase Active Power
P = V × I × PF

Voltage in volts, current in amperes, power factor from 0 to 1. Result in W and kW.

2. Three-Phase Active Power (Line Values)
P = √3 × VL × IL × PF

Use line-to-line voltage (VL) and line current (IL). Result in W and kW.

3. Three-Phase Apparent Power
S = √3 × VL × IL

Result in VA and kVA. No power factor is needed.

4. Three-Phase Reactive Power
Q = √3 × VL × IL × sin(φ)

Enter power factor; sin(φ) = √(1 − PF²). Result in var and kVAr.

5. Transformer Output Power and Losses
Losses = Input Power − Output Power

Enter input and output active power in kW. Values must use the same basis.

Notes
• For three-phase calculations, use line voltage and line current together.
• Power factor must be between 0 and 1.
• Active power is measured in W/kW; apparent power in VA/kVA; reactive power in var/kVAr.
• Losses are valid only when input and output power refer to the same operating condition.

Energy — Formulas & Calculator

Enter your values in the relevant formula box, then tap its Calculate button. The answer appears inside that same box.

1. Energy from Power and Time
E = P × t

Power in watts, time in seconds → energy in joules (J).

2. Energy from Voltage, Current and Time
E = V × I × t

Use volts, amperes and seconds → joules (J).

3. Energy Using Current and Resistance
E = I² × R × t

Current in amperes, resistance in ohms, time in seconds → joules.

4. Energy Using Voltage and Resistance
E = (V² × t) / R

Voltage in volts, resistance in ohms, time in seconds → joules.

5. Energy from Charge and Voltage
E = Q × V

Charge in coulombs and voltage in volts → joules.

6. Electricity Units from Watts and Hours
Energy (kWh) = W × hours / 1000

Result is kWh; 1 kWh equals 1 electricity unit.

7. Electricity Units from Kilowatts and Hours
Energy (kWh) = kW × hours
8. Power from Energy and Time
P = E / t

Energy in joules and time in seconds → watts.

9. DC / Resistive Power
P = V × I

Voltage in volts × current in amperes → watts.

10. DC / Resistive Power from Current and Resistance
P = I² × R
11. DC / Resistive Power from Voltage and Resistance
P = V² / R
12. Single-Phase AC Real Power
P = V × I × PF

Enter power factor (PF) between 0 and 1. Result in watts.

13. Balanced Three-Phase AC Real Power
P = √3 × VL × IL × PF

Use line voltage (V), line current (A), and PF from 0 to 1. Result in watts.

Quick unit guide

Use seconds for joules and hours for kWh. 1 kWh = 1 electricity unit. For cost, use energy in kWh × tariff per unit.

Energy Consumption & Cost Calculator

Consumption Metrics:
• Daily Consumption:
kWh = (Watts × Hours) / 1000

• Financial Cost:
Cost = Total kWh × Rate per kWh

CT / VT Phase Displacement Tool

Angular Transformation Logic:
• Degrees:
deg = Minutes / 60

• Radians:
rad = deg × (π / 180)

• Centiradians:
crad = rad × 100

Convert instrument transformer phase displacement error from minutes into geometric degrees or metric units.

kVAh & Power Factor Calculator

Vector Triangle Summation:
• Apparent Energy:
kVAh = √(kWh² + kVARh²)

• Avg Power Factor:
cos θ = kWh / kVAh

148 Parameter Sweep Matrix

Calculation Logic Reference:
1. Single Pulse Constant Duration (s):
t_s = (3600 × 1000) / (3 × V × I × PF × Pulse Rate)

2. Required Pulses to reach target time limit:
N = ⌈T_target / t_s⌉

3. Actual Test Time (s):
T_act = N × t_s
